title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-11-06
lineage: Sony TC-110 with built-in microphone > Cass > Reel > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: A legendary Capitol Theatre show with soaring jams (Alligator, Caution‑Lovelight) captured on a decent but gritty audience tape.
ai_review.review: The performance is hailed as one of the peak 1970 Dead shows – blistering “Alligator”, a monster “Caution → Lovelight” stretch, plus standout Pigpen harp and acoustic moments.  The recording is an audience (AUD) source; listeners note hiss, boom‑y low end and occasional fuzz, but most agree it’s listenable for its era and the music outweighs the sonic flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Average user rating is ~4.3/5; the show receives strong praise while sound quality draws consistent criticism, leading to a high‑confidence mixed‑sentiment rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Typical 1970 AUD tape – hissy highs, boomy lows, occasional fuzzy passages and source switches between crowd recordings.  Some sections (second‑set jams) are clearer than others; overall listenable with EQ.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic opener leads into a high‑energy electric set; the second set is jam‑heavy with seamless transitions, delivering a relentless, “radioactive” flow that many reviewers cite as a highlight of the Capitol Theatre run.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is described as popping, snap‑crackle soloing, and his smile/fun onstage are repeatedly noted.
band_member_comments.Drums: The Rhythm Devils’ tone gets special praise for driving the jams.
